problem: Kilometre-scale robot navigation needs either accurate SLAM/HD maps, which are costly to build, drift and need loop closure, or end-to-end policies that cannot be steered by high-level goals or handle partial observability.
motivation: Humans navigate large environments with coarse maps such as floorplans and GPS maps plus strong local skills. The paper builds a two-level system, a coarse topological/topometric map planner with a learned intention-conditioned controller, so that no full-environment scanning is needed and localization errors stay tolerable.
key_idea: Plan on a coarse floorplan/GPS-based topological map of Exits to emit discrete intention signals (DLM: turn left/right/forward/stop), and execute them with a memory-augmented, multimodal end-to-end imitation-learned controller (DECISION) that handles local details.
insight: Ablations show that memory placed at multiple spatial scales beats single-level memory, a CNN-LSTM, or no memory. Only the full multi-scale model reaches SR 90 on the pedestrian, blind-spot and elevator tasks, while every baseline gets 0-30 on pedestrian and blind-spot. Local detail belongs in the low-level learned controller, so the map can stay coarse.
method: Two-level topological/topometric map: graph of 'Exit' nodes (indoor, outdoor, stairs, linkway) built manually from downloaded floorplans and OSM/GPS road networks, with Euclidean edge weights; occupancy grids from floorplans are optional. Building takes minutes and needs no mapping pass.
Localization: Elbrus stereo visual odometry with IMU, open-loop and unbounded drift. An Exit counts as reached once the pose falls within its margin, and the pose is reset at each new floorplan.

Intention abstraction: the planned Exit path is converted into a DLM intention (four discrete values, from local path curvature). LPE image intention is described but the paper focuses on DLM because LPE needs accurate localization.
INet controller: pretrained ResNet-50 feature plus a 64-d intention latent, with the intention also selecting one of four control heads; outputs (speed, steering).

DECISION controller: CNN with ConvLSTM memory layers at three abstraction levels, using GroupNorm and channel-wise recurrent plus Monte Carlo dropout. Separate memory cells per intention mode are selected by the planner's mode signal to avoid mode collapse.
Training: teleoperated demonstrations on a Spot robot (410K steps, 7.6 h, with 64K HG-DAGGER steps for the elevator task), resampled to balance modes, trained with TBPTT and AdamW on 112x112 inputs.

setting.backbone: DECISION: shallow CNN with multi-scale ConvLSTM memory layers (trained from scratch); INet: pretrained ResNet-50 with intention head
setting.training_data: 410K time steps (7.6 h) of teleoperated demonstrations on Spot in indoor, semi-outdoor and outdoor environments, including 64K HG-DAGGER steps for the elevator task
setting.observation: monocular RGB (RealSense D435i, resized to 112x112) plus stereo visual odometry/IMU for localization
setting.privileged: hand-specified topological map (Exits and connections) from floorplans and OSM; no pre-built SLAM map

numbers_note: The paper is an unfinished draft (abstract and intro empty, placeholder tables, empty routes/results sections). It has no results on standard benchmarks. The real-robot ablation on custom tasks is not included in the numbers field.
results: On custom real-robot partial-observability tasks (N=10), DECISION reaches SR 90/90/90 on pedestrian, blind-spot and elevator, and CR 98.8/98/95, close to a human operator (SR 90/90/100). Baselines (INet, multi-frame CNN, CNN-LSTM, memory ablations) get SR 0-30 on the first two tasks. The best baseline on elevator is the LateLayer variant with SR 70. Kilometre-scale (~1.5 km) route results are not reported in the text.
limitations: Draft is incomplete: the abstract, intro, large-scale results and noisy-intention tables are missing or placeholders
Exits and edges are specified manually, and visual odometry drift needs pose resets at floor transitions
Evaluation is on custom tasks with small N=10 and no standard-benchmark comparison
